FlexRL assumes conditional independence between PIVs, consider merging or dropping one. #> '2' is the larger source, saved as B; '1' saved as A. fit1 <- StEM( data = prep_data, StEM_iter = 5, StEM_burnin = 2,                gibbs_iter = 5, gibbs_burnin = 2, n_post_sample = 5,               model_dynamics = survival_model("exponential") ) #> FlexRL apply(fit1$alpha$V4[2:5,], 2, mean) #>   intercept          Xe          Xf  #> -0.08812096 -0.57437484 -0.47599521  cond_hazard_params1$V4 #> [1] -0.3566749 -0.5108256 -0.6931472 head(fit1$Delta[fit1$Delta$x > 0.5, ]) #>    i j   x #> 1  1 1 1.0 #> 4  4 4 1.0 #> 5  5 5 1.0 #> 6 77 6 0.8 #> 7  7 7 1.0 #> 8  8 8 1.0  cond_hazard_params2 <- list( V1 = c(), V2 = c(),                               V3 = c(), V4 = log(c(0.3, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5)) ) gen_data <- simulate_data( PIVs_config, n_values, c(150, 200), 100,                             p_mistake, p_missing, cond_hazard_params2, TRUE,                            model_dynamics = survival_model("weibull") ) prep_data <- prepare_data( gen_data$data1, gen_data$data2, "1", "2",                            PIVs_config, TRUE, "entity_id", TRUE ) #> '2' is the larger source, saved as B; '1' saved as A. fit2 <- StEM( data = prep_data, StEM_iter = 5, StEM_burnin = 2,                gibbs_iter = 5, gibbs_burnin = 2, n_post_sample = 5,               model_dynamics = survival_model("weibull")) #> FlexRL apply(fit2$alpha$V4[2:5,], 2, mean) #>   log_shape   intercept          Xe          Xf  #>  0.00925035 -1.18432592  0.14060766 -0.59662506  cond_hazard_params2$V4 #> [1] -1.2039728 -0.3566749 -0.5108256 -0.6931472 head(fit2$Delta[fit2$Delta$x > 0.5, ]) #>      i j   x #> 4    4 4 0.8 #> 6    5 5 0.6 #> 7    6 6 0.8 #> 9  128 7 0.8 #> 10  61 8 1.0 #> 11   9 9 0.8  cond_hazard_params3 <- list( V1 = c(), V2 = c(),                               V3 = c(), V4 = log(c(0.3, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5)) ) gen_data <- simulate_data( PIVs_config, n_values, c(150, 200), 100,                             p_mistake, p_missing, cond_hazard_params3, TRUE,                            model_dynamics = survival_model("gompertz") ) prep_data <- prepare_data( gen_data$data1, gen_data$data2, "1", "2",                            PIVs_config, TRUE, "entity_id", TRUE ) #> '2' is the larger source, saved as B; '1' saved as A. fit3 <- StEM( data = prep_data, StEM_iter = 5, StEM_burnin = 2,                gibbs_iter = 5, gibbs_burnin = 2, n_post_sample = 5,               model_dynamics = survival_model("gompertz")) #> FlexRL apply(fit3$alpha$V4[2:5,], 2, mean) #>           g   intercept          Xe          Xf  #> -1.13048839 -2.14282882 -0.08845059  0.39299854  cond_hazard_params3$V4 #> [1] -1.2039728 -0.3566749 -0.5108256 -0.6931472 head(fit3$Delta[fit3$Delta$x > 0.5, ]) #>      i  j   x #> 3    3  3 1.0 #> 5    6  6 1.0 #> 10 116 11 0.8 #> 11  12 12 1.0 #> 12  13 13 0.8 #> 14  15 15 1.0  cond_hazard_params4 <- list( V1 = c(), V2 = c(),                               V3 = c(), V4 = log(c(0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1)) ) gen_data <- simulate_data( PIVs_config, n_values, c(150, 200), 100,                             p_mistake, p_missing, cond_hazard_params4, TRUE,                            model_dynamics = survival_model("piecewise", cuts = c(1,2,3)) ) prep_data <- prepare_data( gen_data$data1, gen_data$data2, "1", "2",                            PIVs_config, TRUE, "entity_id", TRUE ) #> '2' is the larger source, saved as B; '1' saved as A. fit4 <- StEM( data = prep_data, StEM_iter = 2, StEM_burnin = 1,                gibbs_iter = 2, gibbs_burnin = 1, n_post_sample = 2,               model_dynamics = survival_model("piecewise", cuts = c(1,2,3))) #> FlexRL #> Warning: PIV 'V1', file A hit its mistake bound on 50% of StEM iterations. #>   PIV 'V1', file B hit its mistake bound on 50% of StEM iterations. apply(fit4$alpha$V4, 2, mean) #>        log_h1        log_h2        log_h3        log_h4            Xe  #>  -0.124675252  -1.965644581 -19.676423339  -1.218537916   0.007940481  #>            Xf  #>  -0.224878671  cond_hazard_params4$V4 #> [1] -0.5108256 -0.6931472 -0.9162907 -1.2039728 -1.6094379 -2.3025851 head(fit4$Delta[fit4$Delta$x > 0.5, ]) #>     i j x #> 1   1 1 1 #> 2   2 2 1 #> 3 107 3 1 #> 4   4 4 1 #> 5   5 5 1 #> 6   6 6 1

title: Survival models for the dynamics of a PIV — survival_model
text: Available models (h hazard, lambda = exp(X alpha_cov) proportional-hazards term): "exponential" S(t) = exp(-lambda t); alpha = coefficients X (default, model methodology paper). "weibull" S(t) = exp(-(lambda t)^k) shape k = exp(alpha[1]); alpha = log-shape, coefficients X. "gompertz" h(t) = lambda exp(g t), S(t) = exp(-lambda (exp(g t) - 1) / g) g = alpha[1]; alpha = g, coefficients X. "piecewise" piecewise-constant baseline hazard intervals defined cuts, times lambda; alpha = one log-hazard per interval, coefficients covariates (intercept). "custom" S, n_par init supplied user. every model negative log-likelihood used M-step -sum(Hequal log S + (1 - Hequal) log(1 - S)), Hequal indicates true values linked pair agree. Parameters estimated stats::nlminb() (numerical gradient).

title: FlexRL 1.0.1 (release candidate)
text: Bugs fixed. Performance: Gibbs machinery ~100x faster end--end benchmark problem (review/bench-stem.R, nA=10000, nB=15000, n_links=7500, 22 sweeps: 238.7 s -> 2.29 s); 100k/150k-record problem (75k links, 22 sweeps) serial run takes 88 s threads = 8 brings ~51 s. candidate-pair log-likelihood now plain per-pair vector (nA x nB sparse matrix data-frame row subsetting gone), candidate pairs built single C++ call (buildCandidatePairs()), per-sweep likelihood pieces computed one fused C++ pass (pairLogLik()), sampleL samples joint (H^, H^B) exact O(nval) factorization, kernels draw pre-drawn uniform blocks. sampleD() signature now (S, LLA, LLB, LLL, gamma, nlinkrec, links, threads). gamma single scalar; linkage state passed links, 0-based k x 2 matrix (, B) record pairs (0x2 nothing linked), replacing sumRowD/sumColD arguments — flags derived links still returned. return list gains links (updated 0-based pairs) next linksQ (1-based rows S); loglik dropped inputs (value cancels every acceptance ratio reconstructed internally). simulateD() likewise takes current linksR sumRowD/sumColD; gains threads model_dynamics. global C++ link map — initDeltaMap() Deltafind() — gone: sweep carries state calls, everything needs lives arguments. sampleNL() takes unif argument; sampleL() takes (survivalpSameH, nval, phikA, phikB, eta, unif) returns joint (H^, H^B) matrix. Kernels draw Uniform(0,1) deviates pre-drawn blocks consumed pair position rather calling RNG per draw: given set.seed() realised draws differ <= 1.0.0 (distributions ). OpenMP: per-pair likelihood loops Gibbs kernels parallelised; new threads argument StEM() (default 4; build without OpenMP code runs sequentially regardless). Results bitwise identical thread count. package still builds — runs sequentially — platforms without OpenMP. built-survival models (exponential, Weibull, Gompertz, piecewise) evaluate fused, parallel C++ kernel (survivalS_cpp) instead R-level matrix algebra; custom survival functions unaffected keep working exactly . Values agree previous R implementation ~1e-16 (BLAS rounding); survival_model() objects gain cuts field. Parity verified pre-optimisation implementation pinned permanent regression tests: tests/testthat/test-golden-parity.R compares current kernels golden fixtures generated pre-optimisation build (review/generate-goldens.R, baseline glm-notes @ 4b09088) — likelihoods candidate-pair sets exactly, StEM seed clouds tiny problem’s stationary frequencies Monte-Carlo level. See review/PARITY-REPORT.md.
